parsed.explanation: No criminalisation, no anti-trans statute, no documented police targeting, and foreign passports are the operative documents. Official endorsement of Pride and a 2024 protection instrument that names trans people are positive evidence. Against that: no gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime coverage, so recourse is thin; reported verbal abuse in public medical centres touches a visitor-facing setting; and the 2017 foreign report found no government action on discrimination. Violence is mainly family and community-based, which is local-sphere material, and the 86% figure is from a 57-person self-selected sample, so I give it no weight. A same-sex-read partner has no spousal recognition, a real but open emergency-care and residence gap. Border and facility practice are undocumented, so I do not count them as exposures. Net: reduced risk, held down by thin recourse and the medical-setting friction.
